item.title: Why Pakistan were forced to shift Sri Lanka Test from Lahore to Rawalpindi
item.description: Pakistan have changed the venue of the second Test against Sri Lanka because of worsening smog in Lahore. The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) announced on Tuesday that the second match of the two-Test series will now be played in Rawalpindi instead of Lahore. Rawalpindi is already hosting the first Test of the series. The second match will also be played at the same venue from November 17 to 21. The dates have not been changed. Lahore has been facing poor air quality in recent weeks as heavy smog has covered large parts of Pakistan during the winter season. According to IQAir, a Swiss company that monitors air quality, Lahore is currently the most polluted major city in the world. The poor air quality has forced Pakistan to shift cricket matches to other venues in the past as well. In November 2020, Pakistan moved its limited-overs series against Zimbabwe from Lahore to Rawalpindi because of smog. In December 2022, a Test match between Pakistan and New Zealand was also shifted from Multan to Karachi due to similar air-quality concerns. Despite the change in venue, the second Test between Pakistan and Sri Lanka will take place on the originally scheduled dates. The two teams will play the match in Rawalpindi from November 17 to 21.

item.title: Greg Christodulu steps down as Shenendehowa baseball coach
item.description: Shenendehowa head coach Greg Christodulu is seen during a baseball game against Colonie on Monday, April 13, 2026 in Colonie, N.Y. (Lori Van Buren/Times Union) (Lori Van Buren/Times Union) From the moment Greg Christodulu took as head coach of the Shenendehowa varsity baseball program, his team enjoyed immediate success. Now, his run as the leader of the program has come to an end as he will not be coaching the team for the 2027 season. "He has chosen to retire," Shenendehowa athletic director Lucas LaBarre said. "The (job) post is now up, so (the information) I can tell you is public as the head baseball position has been posted. We will be interviewing (this) week." "I really did want any have pat on the back or cake ceremony. I just want to walk away from it," Christodulu said about the end of his coaching career. "I told them I didn't need a press conference or to talk about it. I really don't have a comment." The eventual replacement for Christodulu will be just the program's fourth head coach since 1956. Don Van Vliet was the first head coach and led Shen to 325 wins. "I knew he was getting close to that time and he has made the decision to retire for both teaching and baseball," LaBarre said. "It is a big loss for us." Christodulu, who claimed his 200th career win in April 2025 with a victory over Saratoga Springs, is a physical education teacher at the high school. He joined the baseball coaching staff in 2003 and ran the JV program. The team compiled a 108-28 record from 2003 to 2009. He then became a varsity assistant coach. Christodulu took over the varsity program in August 2012 from Jim Carrese, who guided Shen to 349 victories during his tenure as coach. Christodulu led the program to six sectional titles - including his first season in 2013, when the Mustangs beat Shaker 3-2 in the final for the program's first area championship since 1996. Christodulu's most recent sectional titles came back-to-back in 2023 and 2024. The program's most prolific season camein 2016 when the team, led by future No. 3 overall MLB draft pick Ian Anderson, captured the Class AA state championship in Binghamton with wins on the same day against West Islip (3-0) and Webster Schroeder (7-6). The 2026 season marked the first time in Christodulu's varsity coaching run that his team experienced a losing record for a full season. The Mustangs dropped a 5-4 Section 2 Class AAA quarterfinal decision against Colonie to finish 7-13. Nine years ago, Shenendehowa and Saratoga Springs became competing for the I-87 Cup trophy to add another layer to the rivalry between the two schools. The Blue Streaks won the first encounter with the trophy up for grabs in 2017 at Shuttleworth Park in Amsterdam, prevailing 5-4 on a walk-off home run by Brian Hart. As an athlete, Christodulu starred in three sports at Gloversville. He played quarterback at Syracuse and football and baseball at the University of Delaware, graduating in 1987. item.title: Grondahl: These Albany rowers in their 80s reunited for a race against time
item.description: Octogenarians Charles Touhey, Dr. Bill Cromie and Phil Hansen in the boathouse of the Albany Rowing Center after reminiscing about their daily pre-dawn rowing workouts and years of entering regattas in the 1980s. (Paul Grondahl/For the Times Union) ALBANY - Three octogenarians sat at a picnic table in front of the Albany Rowing Center boathouse and as the sun slowly set over the Hudson River, the years melted away. They imagined themselves as "the boys in the boat" once again. Two score and more years ago, the trio awoke each morning in the pre-dawn darkness, carried a needle-thin, eight-person shell to the river and pulled the oars in unison, guided by a coxswain's barked cadence. As sunrise burned off morning mist, they found camaraderie and passion in 90 minutes of maximum physical exertion with intense mental focus. "I called it shared suffering," said Dr. Bill Cromie, 83, of Albany, a retired pediatric urologist and former president and CEO of Capital District Physicians' Health Plan. He finished daily rowing practice at 7 a.m., showered quickly and scrubbed in for surgery in the operating room of Albany Medical Center. The no pain, no gain philosophy created a bond that lasted. Cromie, Phil Hansen, 81, and Charles Touhey, 80, spent a couple hours Friday afternoon reminiscing about their glory days as early members of O.A.R.S., Organization of Adirondack Rowers and Scullers, established in 1984 and renamed the Albany Rowing Center. They spent countless hours on the edge of physical agony chasing a transcendent moment known as "the swing." It is the ultimate in synchronicity, when eight rowers guided by a coxswain attain a crescendo of perfectly powered momentum that propels the shell on a cushion of effortless power, with a sense of near-weightlessness, as 16 arms and eight oars move in exquisite rhythm, their blades slicing the water as one through the catch, drive, finish and recovery of the stroke cycle. "The swing" is an almost mystical state that this trio and all competitive scullers aspire to, yet rarely capture - the white whale of crew races. The octogenarians experienced that euphoric feeling in an eight-man shell as rarely as seeing a blue moon. "If you find the swing, it feels totally effortless. It's like shifting a sports car from first to fourth gear and accelerating," Hansen said. The catalyst for their pursuit of "the swing" was the late Albany Mayor Thomas Whalen III, a rowing devotee who sparked a rebirth of the sport on the Hudson with the construction of a boathouse and establishing the Empire State Regatta in 1985 and Head of the Hudson Regatta. Whalen, Cromie and Neil Kaye were prime movers of the effort and soon Hansen and Touhey became core members. Last Friday's gathering was spurred by Princeton alumni Hansen ('66) and Touhey ('68), who helped assemble an octogenarian Princeton alumni eight-man crew team. The La Fabrica talent was one of the few positives from an underwhelming last season for Real Madrid, as he became a regular in the senior setup following his debut under Alvaro Arbeloa in January. Minutes have proven significantly harder to come by for Pitarch this season, but the teenage midfielder continues to remain in the first-team dynamics. Pitarch reflects on his Real Madrid journey Prior to joining Real Madrid’s academy, Pitarch had stints with Leganes and Atletico Madrid’s youth setups. And the 19-year-old starlet revealed that he jumped at the opportunity to sign for Los Blancos the moment he learned about their interest. “I started playing when I was very young, at Atletico’s youth academy; the coach was Pantic,” he explained, before adding: “When the opportunity arose to go to Real Madrid at 16, I didn’t hesitate.” Thiago Pitarch loving life at Real Madrid. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) Pitarch was called up to first-team training from pre-season in the summer of 2025 by Xabi Alonso. Recalling his first experience with the senior setup, the youngster admitted that he was terrified. “I was terrified during my first training session with Real Madrid. In that first training session, I scored a goal from a pass by Mbappe; I have to ask for that video,” Thiago recalled. item.title: Barcelona set for potential €10m windfall as Chelsea and Man United show interest in former striker – report
item.description: Barcelona set for potential €10m windfall as Chelsea and Man United show interest in former striker – report Barcelona could benefit financially from Vitor Roque’s potential departure from Palmeiras in the January transfer window, with Manchester United, Everton, Chelsea and Tottenham monitoring the Brazilian striker. According to SPORT , the Catalan club are following developments closely because they retained a percentage of the forward’s future transfer fee when selling him in February 2025. Roque has rebuilt his reputation in Brazil after struggling to establish himself during his brief spell at Barcelona. His performances for Palmeiras have attracted interest from England, and a move back to European football could now generate a significant financial return for his former club . Manchester United join Premier League race for Vitor Roque Everton, Chelsea and Tottenham are among the clubs reportedly interested in the 21-year-old, with Manchester United recently joining the list of potential suitors. The four Premier League sides are said to have made contact with the player’s representatives to understand the conditions required to negotiate a transfer. Four Premier League teams are interested in Vitor Roque. (Photo by Alexandre Schneider/Getty Images) Roque’s agent, Andre Cury, has confirmed that several European clubs are monitoring his client, stating, “There are many European clubs interested in Vitor.” However, interest does not necessarily mean that negotiations are advanced. This is because Palmeiras are reluctant to lose one of their important attacking players and, with Roque contracted until December 2029, are in a strong position to demand a substantial fee. Palmeiras demand €50m as Barcelona retain sell-on clause According to the report, Palmeiras have set their minimum asking price at €50 million, and that valuation is particularly significant for Barcelona because of the financial conditions included in Roque’s departure. Barcelona sold the striker for €25.5 million in fixed payments, with additional variables, but retained a percentage of his future transfer rights. Barcelona stand to gain from Roque’s potential move. (Photo by Franklin Jacome/Getty Images) The arrangement provides the Catalan club with a 10% share for a sale below €35 million, 15% between €35 million and €40.99 million, and 20% for a transfer worth at least €41 million. Consequently, a €50 million sale would generate €10 million for Barcelona, provided the reported terms are applied to the transfer fee. Deco could benefit from Roque’s revival in Brazil Barcelona sporting director Deco will have reason to follow the situation closely, as he was involved in bringing Roque to the club, but the forward struggled to secure a regular role before returning to Brazil. item.description: 'I'm very disappointed': Former Australia coach, part of Sandpapergate tour, rejects Usman Khawaja's claims as 'absolutely false' originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: Graeme Hick has called Usman Khawaja's claim that the whole squad knew about the sandpaper plot "absolutely false". Australia's former batting coach says he first learned of it from the big screen in Cape Town. Khawaja has alleged a coaching staff member encouraged Cameron Bancroft to use sandpaper. Graeme Hick rejects Usman Khawaja's Sandpapergate claims Usman Khawaja's allegation that every member of Australia's 2018 touring party knew about the ball-tampering plan has now been contradicted by the man who was the side's batting coach at the time. Graeme Hick has dismissed it outright. Hick, who held the role from 2016 to 2020, took issue not only with the substance of the claim but with the fact that it was made about everyone at once. "I have seen the various statements around the coaches, and I'm very disappointed with the broad nature of them," he told the Sydney Morning Herald . He then addressed Khawaja's central line directly. "Khawaja puts it simply: "It was all of us. Not the batters, not the bowlers, not the staff. All of us. To me, what Khawaja is implying here is absolutely false," Hick explained. "In regard to any discussions around the ball tampering in Port Elizabeth or Cape Town that took place, I will say in true honesty that I did not hear or know anything." His account of when he found out matches the version Cricket Australia's investigation settled on in 2018. "My first knowledge of all this was, like many, when it appeared on the big screen in Cape Town, as I was sat on the outside balcony at the time," Hick said in his statement. item.description: SEATTLE, WA - NOVEMBER 07: Rocco Becht #3 of the Penn State Nittany Lions hands the ball to teammate Cam Wallace #26 during a game between the Penn State Nittany Lions and Washington Huskies on November 7, 2026 at Husky Stadium in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Henry Rodenburg/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images I wrote after the Purdue game asking if I could has run game , and it appears after playing Washington that I can, in fact, has run game. Against the Boilermakers the Penn State rushing game came to life. Carson Hansen, who was much maligned earlier in the season, ripped off 96 yards on 17 carries, while Cam Wallace broke out with 135 yards on 22 carries, each with a touchdown to boot. It seemed the backs were finally starting to gel with the offensive line – which itself was utilizing more gap blocking – and things were getting sorted out. All told the team racked up 269 yards on the ground. But surely they couldn’t keep it up against Washington, right? The Huskies were infinitely better than Purdue, so the success on the ground was just a blip on an otherwise uneventful season for the rushing attack. How about Hansen toting the rock 14 times for 119 yards and a TD, and Wallace taking his 7 carries for 56 yards and a score? Both backs came in over 8 yards per carry on the day. I’d say they’ve certainly figured things out. Given the passing game woes, which goes from converting deep bomb after deep bomb to a seeming inability to complete a screen pass, seeing the running backs reliably move the chains is a breath of fresh air. So now, the only real question is what do we call this two-headed RB monster? Hansen will never be mistaken for a speedy back, but will certainly plow into defenders and drag them for a few yards. Wallace, meanwhile, has the most explosiveness on the team, and can turn a small seam into a 40-yard touchdown run. If Carson Hansen is Thunder, then Cam Wallace must be Lightning. item.description: Enzo Fernandez and Elliot Anderson both cost Manchester City more than £100m in the summer [Getty Images] The ongoing international break will give Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca much-needed time to fix the growing issues in his squad. The Italian made a dream start after taking over from Pep Guardiola in the summer, leading the club to a record seven consecutive victories at the beginning of the Premier League season. But three consecutive defeats have followed as they have fallen six points adrift of league leaders Arsenal, who are looking in imperious form as they aim to retain their title. In September, it was announced that City had been found guilty of breaking the Premier League's financial rules, and matches have continued as the club await the outcome of their appeal. With possible sanctions hanging over them, is City's recent league form down to psychological issues or are there tactical problems Maresca needs to address? Maresca's dream start turns into nightmare as title hopes hit Property, football and politics: The links between Manchester and Abu Dhabi explained Renowned sports psychologist Dr Paul McCarthy has 25 years' experience working in the industry with top clubs in England, Scotland, Germany and France. McCarthy works on the personal and professional lives of players and says both contribute to how well they perform on the pitch, with the need to "piece together a jigsaw" when situations become disrupted. "Players are like everyone else - they talk about what is going on in their own lives and things that are topical, especially about uncertain events," McCarthy tells BBC Sport. "It generates communication with a lot of stories and rumour and over time if there are enough losses, there often becomes a reduced collective efficacy. "A collective efficacy is a squad's belief in their ability to do what they need to do [to win] and because of their success in the past, that is often shaken a little by consecutive losses." 'Uncertainty leads to a lack of perceived control' City were sitting pretty at the top of the table after a flawless start, but have dropped to third - behind Arsenal and Brighton. item.description: Tigers Head Coach Brian Kelly, LSU Tigers take on the Texas A&M Aggies. © Imagn Former LSU head coach Brian Kelly believes the College Football Playoff’s planned expansion to 24 teams in 2027 will bring the biggest shift in how teams define success. Kelly believes winning a conference championship may no longer be the ultimate goal for programs. Instead, securing a place in the expanded playoff field will become their primary focus. Speaking on SiriusXM, Kelly explained how the new format could reshape college football. “You don’t have to worry about winning the conference championship. You need to be one of the 24 teams. And so that’s a paradigm shift in terms of what you’re looking at, in terms of building your football team,” Kelly said. Kelly thinks the expanded playoff will give more programs a realistic opportunity to compete for a national championship. As per the new 24-team format, the playoff field will include the four Power Four conference champions, the highest-ranked Group of Six champion, and 19 teams selected based on the committee’s final rankings. That structure will be significantly beneficial for programs that traditionally struggled to compete financially and recruit at the same level as other teams with bigger budgets. “So it’s now a lot different in terms of what your ultimate goal is. And that’s get in the playoffs,” he added. Alabama’s Ranking Raises Questions About the CFP Selection Criteria The current playoff selection process shows why conference championships and head-to-head results don’t tell the full story. Alabama went up from No. 5 to No. 3 in the CFP rankings despite having two losses. Committee chair Hunter Yurachek defended the decision by saying it’s because of the Crimson Tide’s strength of schedule and four quality wins. “They’re number one in their record strength, number one in their schedule strength. They have four of what we call quality wins, because we continue to call that the win against Mississippi State earlier in the year when they had Kamario Taylor on their team. They were four and zero. Alabama went there and won that game. So Alabama, we believe, deserves to be the number three team in the country,” committee chair Hunter Yurachek said on ESPN. Alabama’s ranking also placed it above Tennessee, despite the Volunteers defeating the Crimson Tide earlier in the season. Yurachek explained that the committee considers the overall resume rather than relying only on head-to-head results. item.title: Stephen A. Smith says Sean McVay has done something ‘inexcusable’ with the LA Rams
item.description: Photo by David Crane/MediaNews Group/Los Angeles Daily News via Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams have had a mixed 2026/27 season so far after having a lot of hype around them ahead of the campaign. Going into Week 10 of the season they have a 5-4 record and are third in the NFC West. Now, Stephen A. Smith has gone on a rant about Rams coach Sean McVay, first taking issue with how late his team flew to Australia to face the San Francisco 49ers at the start of the season. Speaking via NFL on ESPN , he said: “I have to say to Sean McVay, what has happened to you? What’s happened to you? I think he’s an elite coach. I think he’s big time. He’s a brilliant dude, next level with football, a wonderful dude to talk to, the whole bit. Got nothing but love for him. “I don’t know what the h*** has happened to him this year. You go to Melbourne, Australia, and land 28 hours before kickoff. The 49ers were there for a week. For some reason, you’re the only human being alive, the only adult that I’ve ever known that didn’t take into consideration jet lag and the kind of impact that will have on you.” Stephen A. Smith suggests handling of Puka Nacua amid injuries is ‘some inexcusable stuff’ After that, he questioned the handling of Puka Nacua on the back of his injury issues, suggesting that putting him in a ‘jet-sweep situation’ is ‘inexcusable stuff’. Smith continued: “Sunday, a jet sweep for Puka Nacua, who’s had injuries, on a third-and-11, I believe it was. I mean, what are you calling a jet sweep for? For him? “This is the dude that was healthy enough to play but didn’t want to play because he wasn’t 100%. And you’re going to put him in a position to get compromised health-wise by something other than running a route out in the deep parts of a football field, when your options, because Davante Adams ain’t in there… Because I have to look up these names, because I’ll be d***** if I know them. Konata Mumpfield, right? “Tutu Atwell, you know, Jordan Whittington, Xavier Smith. You ever heard of those names? I mean, y’all get paid to cover football for a living, and you’ve got to look those names up. We don’t know those people. No disrespect to you. I’m quite sure you can play, but we don’t know you. You understand? So, I’m like, what the h*** is going on? “This is what you’ve got to rely upon, you know this, and you’re going to put Puka Nacua in a jet-sweep situation. This is some inexcusable stuff. I don’t know what the h*** is going on with Sean McVay. I love Sean McVay. I don’t understand what has happened to him. I think it’s a little bit too much California sunshine.” The Rams are now due to take on the 3-6 Arizona Cardinals on Sunday, November 15. Should they lose that tie, they will have already matched their losses from the entirety of 2025 when they finished the regular season 12-5. Bassey, meanwhile, has developed into a regular presence at Fulham since arriving from Ajax in 2023. The Nigerian defender offers physical strength and versatility, having also featured at left-back during his career. However, being included on United’s shortlist does not necessarily indicate that either player is close to a move. The report identifies them as possible targets, with no formal bids or negotiations mentioned. item.title: Damian Lillard is back and Ja Morant is here. How exactly is this going to work? | Bill Oram
item.description: In the history of basketball, we have certainly seen some why-would-they-do-that? pairings. Jerseys and sleeves. Kawhi Leonard and a tree sponsorship. Utah and “the Jazz.” Once, there was even Detlef Schrempf and a headband, if you can believe that. Ja Morant and Damian Lillard? We’re about to find out if they belong on such a list. Because of all the things you might have said the Trail Blazers needed as they prepared to welcome Lillard back after making a playoff run without him, a slight-of-stature ball-dominant guard with a questionable jump shot would not have topped anyone’s list. Depth on the wing? Yes. Shooting? Definitely. Defense? Always. Morant doesn’t particularly address any of those, and yet, he’s here, a dynamic two-time All-Star in need of a second act, being paid a team-high $42.1 million to play the same position as not just Lillard, but Jrue Holiday and Scoot Henderson. Heck, the Blazers’ most valuable point guard last season was forward Deni Avdija. “I’m sure there will be questions about fit,” General Manager Joe Cronin said Monday. Uh, yeah. The Blazers have little more than three weeks before the regular season begins in which to figure that out. At the team’s annual media day on Monday, Morant appeared in a fresh white No. 1 Trail Blazers jersey. It’s happening. “It’s easy for people to be like, ‘Man how is this going to work,’” Lillard offered. “‘They can’t do this, they can’t do that.’ But being on the floor with them … we can be a dangerous team and I really believe that.” The onus is on the Trail Blazers starting this month to prove that they bet right in acquiring Morant. And that pairing him with Lillard isn’t the boondoggle conventional wisdom suggests it will be. Lillard noted how many teams that succeeded in the playoffs last year, think San Antonio with its four point guards, relied on numerous playmakers. To his credit, Morant said he would be comfortable coming off the bench, if necessary. But they would not be the first NBA team to fall into the trap of believing they are capable of adjusting or that they will be comfortable sacrificing. It isn’t uncommon to see players in those situations default to familiar habits and sensibilities once the season is underway or struggles come. That’s what made a lot of the positive energy around what sure seems like an awkward roster ring so hollow. We’re going to need to see it to believe it. item.title: Oregon star edge rusher Teitum Tuioti out for the season
item.description: EUGENE — One of Oregon football’s most important defensive players is done for the season. Ducks senior defensive end Teitum Tuioti suffered a season-ending knee injury in Oregon’s 41-28 win over Ohio State , Dan Lanning announced on Monday. “Teitum has been unbelievable for us this year, and every year he’s been here,” Lanning said. “Just watching him grow as a player and person has been a lot of fun for us. But unfortunately Teitum’s done for the year, he had a knee injury, he’ll end up having surgery.” Tuioti was among the Ducks’ leaders in tackles with 44, and ranked second on the team in sacks with 5.5 on the season. The former Sheldon High School star sits at No. 8 all-time for Oregon with 22.5 sacks across his four seasons, providing steady leadership on a talented and experienced defensive front. In the win over the Buckeyes, he also showed off his arm: Tuioti completed a pass to fellow defensive end Matayo Uiagalelei on a memorable fake punt which shifted momentum in the game. “I hate it for him, because (the injury) was a routine, weird play that it happened on,” Lanning said. “He left it on the line there on the field, and I don’t know if he’ll get another chance to play as an Oregon football player, but whoever gets to have that guy on their team in the future is gonna be really, really lucky.” Should Tuioti forgo his fifth year of eligibility and enter the NFL Draft, he is a projected second- or third-round pick according to some mock drafts. item.title: Lanning: Stewart incident 'didn't match our standard'
item.description: EUGENE — After Oregon wide receiver Evan Stewart was booked in Springfield Municipal Jail early Sunday morning on DUII charges, Ducks coach Dan Lanning addressed the situation at his weekly press conference Monday. “There was an incident this weekend that didn’t match our standard here in our program,” Lanning said. “There will be an appropriate action taken. Still gathering some details with what that situation looks like. But that would be handled internally. I’m not gonna respond to any other questions about that. We’re gonna handle that with our guys. “There’s an expectation of what you have to... how you have to act, and how you need to perform in our program. Kind of overshadows the success that we had on Saturday, which is disappointing, but that will be handled by us internally. I’m not going to speak on it publicly.” When Lanning was asked a follow-up question about a rumored speeding incident involving other Oregon football players, for which there haven’t been any confirmed arrests, he said, “I was talking about the same thing when I first addressed it.” This is also the second instance of an Oregon football team member facing DUII charges in the past year. In April, running backs coach Ra’Shaad Samples allegedly backed his Ford F-150 into a parked car outside a bar in Eugene. His next court date is Oct. 27. An arraignment for Stewart in his DUII case hasn’t been set, as official charges haven’t been filed to Springfield Municipal Court as of Monday evening, according to court records. Stewart leads the Ducks this season with 27 catches for 352 yards and four touchdowns. He missed Saturday’s win over Nebraska due to an undisclosed injury. Oregon (4-2, 2-1 Big Ten) is preparing for a road game at Illinois (3-3, 1-2) at 12 p.m. PT this coming Saturday. item.title: Who will call plays for Oregon after Mehringer's firing?
item.description: EUGENE — After firing first-year offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer seven games into the 2026 season, Dan Lanning shared Oregon ’s plans for filling his role moving forward at his weekly press conference Monday night. Offensive assistant Jay Johnson will lead offensive playcalling for the Ducks going forward, Lanning said. “He has a lot of experience as a play-caller, was with me in Georgia when we were part of the national championship team,” Lanning said. “Went on to have a lot of success in Colorado and Michigan State. He’s gonna lead the efforts there with the offensive staff, but it’ll still be a collaborative effort, with a lot of the work that we do. “He’s also coming in with a different perspective, a different view, not being with us the last few years, where he can provide a couple things that might be different than what we’ve done.” Mehringer, previously the tight ends coach for the Ducks, is the first assistant coach Lanning has fired in his tenure at Oregon, which began in 2022. The Ducks’ offensive decision-making was at the center of intense criticism over the past three weeks, during which Oregon averaged just 14 points per game and lost twice to UCLA and Illinois. Lanning spoke to the human element of letting Mehringer go. “They see the football coach, right? That’s also an unbelievable dad. A great husband,” Lanning said. “The guy’s been part of our staff for the last five years, that’s done some really good things here, and I think all of us feel like we shoulder some of the blame. item.title: Caster Semenya rules out role with South African athletics: 'I will not work with snakes'
item.description: Two-time Olympic gold medallist Caster Semenya has ruled out an ambassadorial or leadership role within South African athletics, saying she “will not work with snakes”. Semenya was assigned female at birth but was born with differences of sexual development (DSD), meaning she has higher than usual levels of testosterone for a woman. A three-time world 800m champion, she has spent much of her career - since winning her first world title as a teenager in 2009 - engaged in a battle with World Athletics and sport’s highest court over her eligibility to compete in the elite female category. Rules introduced by the sport’s governing body in 2018 meant the South African could not compete without taking medication to reduce her testosterone levels, which she refused to do, and she lost an appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (Cas), arguing the ruling was discriminatory, the following year. Subsequent appeals have also gone against her, although the European Court of Human Rights (ECHR) ruled in her favour after she brought a case against the Swiss government, which was deemed to have failed to protect her rights, in 2023. The 35-year-old has now ruled herself out of running for election for the Athletics South Africa (ASA) board, saying the federation failed her, and similarly dismissed the idea of ambassadorial role for the South African Sports Confederation and Olympic Committee (SASCOC), which is bidding to host the 2036 or 2040 Olympic Games. Semenya told South African outlet SABC Sport: “I have been betrayed so many times by the very same people. I don't see myself sitting at a table with an enemy. I am going to be honest; I am speaking just for myself. I have no interest in any position or any organization at this moment. “I am not really interested in an organization because they use you as bait, so I don't want to be in a space where I need to answer to someone.” Barring a brief spell running over 5,000m Semenya has since stopped competing and turned to coaching, as well as setting up the Caster Semenya Foundation, which encourages children and communities from impoverished areas to get into sport. She added: “I want to fix my own ship, which is Masai Athletics Club, the Caster Semenya Foundation, which is my priority, and my athletes. “So when it comes to national and international leadership, at the moment I will pause it because I don't see myself working with snakes.”

item.title: France captain Kylian Mbappé set to miss Italy game
item.description: France captain Kylian Mbappé set to miss Italy game Kylian Mbappé (27) looks set to miss France’s UEFA Nations League meeting against Italy tomorrow after feeling discomfort in his hamstring, according to a report from L’Équipe . The publication reported earlier today that the Real Madrid forward was absent from first-team training ahead of this afternoon’s flight to Milan. He is France’s fourth injury concern of this international break. Aurélien Tchouaméni, Pierre Kalulu, and Marcus Thuram have all already withdrawn from the side. The Real Madrid forward was also forced to withdraw early from the last international camp, Zinédine Zidane’s first as manager of Les Bleus. Mbappé could, however, yet participate for France during this current camp. Whilst L’Équipe understands that it is likely that he misses out against Italy on Thursday, it is not thought that the issue is serious. item.title: Newcastle United ready to battle Sunderland in the race for forward
item.description: Newcastle United ready to battle Sunderland in the race for forward Newcastle Scouts Watch Dion Beljo Newcastle United have done the sensible thing here. They have looked, checked, and looked again. According to TeamTalk, club scouts were at the Stadium of Light to watch Dion Beljo as Dinamo Zagreb beat Sunderland 2-0, and the Croatian forward duly did what centre-forwards are paid to do, he scored. That matters. Plenty of strikers can look tidy in clips, rack up flattering numbers in weaker stretches, or disappear when the level rises. Beljo had Premier League eyes on him and still delivered. The report states that “Newcastle and Leeds were both represented on Wearside to watch Beljo in action against Sunderland”, which tells you this was part of a serious information-gathering exercise rather than idle curiosity. Beljo’s output is the headline for a reason. He now has “17 goals in 17 games” this season and an overall senior return of “115 notches from 269 games”. Those are hard numbers, and clubs tend to trust hard numbers more than hype. TeamTalk also notes that Beljo “has been in sensational form for Dinamo”, a fair summary for a striker who appears to be building momentum at exactly the right moment in the market. IMAGO Beljo Transfer Race Growing Fast This is not a one-club chase. Manchester United, Tottenham Hotspur, Everton, Brighton and Brentford have all been credited with interest, while Sunderland are also said to be paying attention after getting a close-up look themselves. In other words, Newcastle are entering a crowded room, and crowded rooms tend to raise prices. Still, there is logic in Newcastle’s interest. TeamTalk says the club “are seeking more of a presence up front” and want to strengthen Matthias Jaissle’s attacking options. That checks out. Squad building is not about collecting names, it is about profile, availability and role. If Beljo offers size, penalty-box instincts and current form, then he fits the brief of an extra forward who can change games and absorb minutes across a long season. The key line in all this may be that clubs are “gathering information on Croatian hotshot”. That is usually where real transfer business starts. Before bids come the background checks, live viewings, tactical fit discussions and financial modelling. Newcastle have clearly moved into that phase. Why Newcastle Interest Makes Sense There is another point worth making. Watching a player against English opposition is useful, even in European competition, because it gives recruiters a cleaner reference point. Beljo facing Sunderland and scoring in a 2-0 win offered exactly that. As the report puts it, “His latest strike against Sunderland will only have strengthened his reputation, particularly given the number of clubs keeping a close eye on his development.” Newcastle will also know that January deals become awkward when too many clubs are involved. item.title: No. 2 Maryland field hockey’s Maddie Vasilios is the epitome of a student-athlete
item.description: No. 2 Maryland field hockey’s Maddie Vasilios is scoring goals, internships and praise from those around her. Her head coach, Missy Meharg, summed her up perfectly. “She is absolutely everybody’s go-to person on the team to feel good, to laugh and to get that confidence from a friend, from a Terp and from a senior,” Meharg said. “The cool thing about Maddie right now is that she is playing the best hockey she has ever played since she has been here.” Field hockey is undoubtedly one of the most important parts of Vasilios’ life. This season, the senior has set career highs in starts, minutes, goals and shots for one of the top-ranked Division I field hockey teams. However, she has made sure to spread her wings elsewhere. Ever since arriving in College Park, the Clarksville, Maryland, native has put herself in the best position to succeed after graduation. “I’ve always been having the mindset of what’s next, post-graduation and after college,” Vasilios said. “I think my parents and my brother have a huge impact on that, just making sure that I had a plan for postgrad.” Like her father and brother, Vasilios is hoping to pursue a career in the financial industry. So far, she has already completed two internships: one as a commercial banking intern with WesBanco and the other as an audit intern with Ellin & Tucker. Both positions were facilitated by her involvement in Maryland Made, the University of Maryland’s student-athlete development program. It has three pillars: career readiness, leadership education, and self-discovery. “It’s really anything that’s not sport and not school,” said Colby Wilson, assistant director of student-athlete development. “It’s really helping our students be who they are and know who they are, and then go do what they want with that.” Vasilios got involved with Maryland Made as soon as she could, joining the Kubasik First Impact Program in the spring of her freshman year. Her involvement in Kubasik kept her coming back for the other programs Maryland Made had to offer. “I just loved being involved and getting to meet other athletes from other teams and hear their story,” Vasilios said. “I think it helped me figure out what I wanted to do postgrad because they’re figuring it out as well as me.” Since completing Kubasik, Vasilios has also participated in the Gossett Fellows, Leadership Academy and inTERPship programs. It was inTERPship that helped place her at WesBanco, and her involvement there introduced her to the Ellin & Tucker position she held this past summer. However, her favorite part of Maryland Made has been her participation in the Student-Athlete Advisory Committee. “We get together once a month at these meetings, and sometimes it’s like, ‘What can we do better?’” she said. “We get to bring these ideas to the athletic department, to Jim Smith and Diana [Sabau], and we get to voice our opinions.” A busy schedule could prove challenging for Vasilios, especially when it comes to pursuing her postgraduate passions.

item.description: Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images Joel Embiid and the Philadelphia 76ers dropped to 9-3 in this 2026-27 NBA season after a 123-101 blowout loss to the Boston Celtics at Xfinity Mobile Arena on Tuesday. All the talk going into this game was about Jaylen Brown and Jayson Tatum , and the former getting revenge against the Celtics for trading him, but it was someone else who shone against his former team. Paul George erupted for 36 points (14-22 FG), five rebounds, and one assist against the 76ers, but Embiid didn’t seem too surprised by his former teammate’s performance in his postgame press conference . “He played well,” Embiid said, via PHLY Sports. “He came in here, and that’s what he’s been doing all season. He’s healthy, he’s in a good space mentally. So yeah, I mean, he’s been playing well all season, and he just did what he was doing all season.” George, whom the Celtics acquired for Brown in the summer, is definitely having a good season, and this is the best we’ve seen him play since his time with the Los Angeles Clippers . The nine-time All-Star struggled with injuries during his two seasons with the 76ers, but is doing well physically and mentally on his new team. Now, Tatum and Brown’s relationship had evidently broken down by the time their partnership ended in the summer, but that’s not the case here. Embiid spoke about having a special relationship with George and threw a subtle jab at Tatum in the process. ‘Obviously, Paul is great,” Embiid said. “Off the court, we have a special relationship. Families are close, especially both of our kids. Actually, all of our kids. So yeah, I mean, I love him. I think that’s why I’m extremely happy for him. He’s healthy; he’s playing well. He’s been, from the start of the season, you see what he did tonight; you can kind of say he’s been the best player, to a certain level. “So, yeah, extremely happy for him, proud of him,” Embiid added. “Obviously, we have a good relationship outside of this whole thing, and that’s what matters.” George has been great, but has he been the Celtics’ best player over Tatum? item.title: You are Scotland boss Pocognoli - what would you do?
item.description: [Getty Images] Sebastien Pocognoli's first camp in charge of Scotland ended in gloomy fashion last month as Slovenia deservedly won 2-1 at Hampden. The Belgian head coach has the chance to bounce back when his side face North Macedonia in Glasgow's southside on Friday, live on the BBC. Scott McTominay, Kieran Tierney and Che Adams are all back in the national team squad for the closing Nations League double-header, which ends with a trip to Switzerland on Monday. Put yourself in Pocognoli's shoes and pick your XI with our team selector below, while we have picked out some of the key selection dilemmas. Best set-up with McTominay return? McTominay is sure to make his first appearance under Pocognoli, but where will the Belgian deploy the Napoli star? The 29-year-old has been sitting slightly deeper in midfield for his club this season but has still managed five goals in 11 outings. Pocognoli used a 3-4-2-1 or 3-4-1-2 formation across his first four games and McTominay could well be used with John McGinn behind a central striker, given the duo's impressive strike rate at international level. Billy Gilmour and Lewis Ferguson were the starting central midfielders in all of Pocognoli previous matches, so is that an established long-term pairing or will Ryan Christie finally get the chance to show what he can do in the area where he has excelled with Bournemouth in recent years? Of course, McTominay and McGinn are options in the middle of the pitch too. Gannon-Doak at wing-back? The width is almost certainly going to come from wing-backs despite an unconvincing beginning to Pocognoli's preferred method. Skipper Andy Robertson is a dead cert to start on the left as he closes in on the nation's caps record currently held by Sir Kenny Dalglish. Ben Gannon-Doak started the last two games on the right but the little winger is not a natural fit in the position. However, he was a dangerous attacking outlet in the 2-0 win away to North Macedonia and may be favourite to keep the jersey for an evening when Scotland are expected to have the lion's share of possession. item.title: 'Crazy' I'll get to 'knock my boss out' - Doumbe
item.description: Cedric Doumbe (right) switched to MMA from kickboxing in 2021 [Getty Images] Cedric Doumbe says it is "crazy" he will get the chance to "face my boss and knock him out" when he fights Jake Paul in Dubai on 24 December. Doumbe is signed to the Professional Fighters League (PFL) - an MMA organisation that Paul's Most Valuable Promotions merged with in July. The pair will fight on Christmas Eve in Paul's first bout since being stopped by former world heavyweight champion Anthony Joshua last December. In a news conference in Paris to promote the event, Cameroonian-born Frenchman Doumbe thanked MVP co-founder Nakisa Bidarian for his role in setting up the fight against Paul. "I want to thank Nakisa. He's the boss. And Jake, he's the boss, too. I want to thank Nakisa, because that's the first time I will face my boss and knock him out," said Doumbe. "My boss will pay me to knock him out. That's crazy. We never see that before." The fight against 29-year-old American Paul is a professionally sanctioned eight-round cruiserweight boxing bout with the fighters using 10oz gloves. Paul, who is a social media influencer turned professional fighter, has won 12 of his 14 fights as a professional, with his two defeats coming against Tommy Fury and Joshua. Doumbe, 34, is a former kickboxing world champion who has won two of his three fights since joining the PFL in 2023. Despite having just one professional boxing bout to his name, which he won in 2015, Doumbe says he's "watching videos on Netflix" instead of training for the fight because he regards Paul as a "joke". "I do nothing. I just watch videos on Netflix. I just want this fight, this clown fight. I have everything to beat this guy," said Doumbe. "This guy is a joke. He's a very great YouTuber, but he's not a fighter. He's not even a good boxer. I just need to lose weight to face this guy, that's why I'm training now." Paul had to have two titanium plates fitted and some teeth removed after having his jaw broken by Joshua - an injury which left his career in doubt. Last week Paul said on social media he would retire if he lost to Doumbe, before confirming his plans in the news conference. "I'm 100% retiring if I lose to this guy. For sure," said Paul. "He's never been in there with someone like me in boxing. It's a completely different sport, that's what he doesn't understand. "I know he's going to bring a tough fight, but it's just not going to be enough, and that's it at the end of the day." item.title: Endrick to Portugal? Sporting boss Paulo Fonseca plots sensational Real Madrid transfer reunion
item.description: FBL-FRA-CUP-LYON-LENS - AFP Real Madrid striker Endrick could be set for a January departure as Sporting CP plot an ambitious winter move. Newly appointed manager Paulo Fonseca has reportedly urged the Portuguese club to secure a reunion with the Brazilian forward ahead of the second half of the season. Endrick considers Real Madrid exit Endrick is facing an increasingly uncertain future at Madrid as the January transfer window approaches. According to AS , the young forward is expected to leave the Spanish capital this winter in search of better opportunities. The 20-year-old attacker has found it difficult to secure a regular starting role this season. He has been restricted to just seven appearances across all competitions, managing to find the back of the net on only one occasion. With playing time severely limited, a mid-season departure is now viewed as the most logical step. Sporting have stepped forward to offer the Brazilian an immediate escape route from his frustrating situation in Madrid. Sporting and Fonseca push for deal The main catalyst behind this potential winter transfer is newly appointed Sporting manager Fonseca . The same report claims that Fonseca has made the Madrid forward a primary target and has directly asked his board to complete the signing in January. Fonseca views the Brazilian as a crucial addition to his new squad in Portugal. The club hierarchy have listened to their coach and have already initiated formal steps to welcome the player to Lisbon in the upcoming window. A move to Sporting would allow Endrick to reunite with a manager he knows extremely well. Fonseca previously recruited the talented attacker during his spell at Lyon last season, leading to a highly fruitful collaboration between the pair. Champions League draw and guaranteed minutes The prospect of linking up with his former Lyon boss is a significant factor for Endrick. Rejoining a coach who completely understands his profile and tactical strengths could provide the perfect environment to restart his season. Furthermore, Sporting can offer the immense appeal of Champions League football. Continuing to test himself in Europe's premier club competition is expected to weigh heavily in the player's final decision. Above all else, Endrick is prioritising a destination that can guarantee him substantial playing time. After a difficult few months at Santiago Bernabeu, the forward is determined to join a project where he will be a central figure. Transfer negotiations and Italian competition Sporting will not have a free run at the Madrid star, as AS Roma are also actively courting the player. The Italian outfit remain firmly in the race and could complicate the Portuguese club's transfer plans. Regarding the structure of the deal, a straightforward loan move remains a highly feasible option for all parties. A temporary switch would allow Endrick to gain vital experience while remaining tied to his parent club.

item.title: Roman Anthony Injury Update: Red Sox CBO Outlines Recovery Plan for $130M Boston Star
item.description: Roman Anthony. © USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Boston Red Sox chief baseball officer Craig Breslow provided an encouraging update on Roman Anthony’s right hand and wrist injury. At Monday’s MLB general managers’ meeting in Las Vegas, Breslow said Anthony’s injury is taking longer to recover from than expected. Anthony, who is signed to an eight-year, $130 million contract, is expected to recover during the offseason. On Tuesday, Breslow joined NESN’s 310 To Left podcast and shared Anthony’s offseason recovery plan. “Yeah, he’s in the midst of, you know, just a period of time where we wanted him to rest and just minimize any of the stress that he might put on his wrist,” Breslow said. “He’s going to be evaluated in a few weeks, at which point we’re hopeful that he can start to take on a strengthening program and get some of the range of motion back before ultimately starting a hitting progression.” Anthony initially injured his right ring finger on May 4 against the Detroit Tigers. He suffered a partially torn carpometacarpal (CMC) ligament, which connects the base of his right ring finger to his wrist. The Red Sox star missed nearly four months before returning on Aug. 30. Anthony’s injury resurfaced during Game 1 of the AL Wild Card Series against the Yankees on September 29. The subsequent imaging revealed new muscle strains in his right wrist, leading to Anthony’s removal from the postseason roster. Later, the Red Sox star admitted that when he first returned in August, he still felt discomfort in his hand, but he risked playing through the injury. Red Sox Rule Out Surgery For Roman Anthony While Craig Breslow admitted that the diagnosis has not changed for Roman Anthony as of now, the need for surgery has been ruled out. Breslow cited Anthony’s multiple follow-up appointments and imaging tests and revealed that the Red Sox outfielder will not need any offseason procedure. “Yeah, he’s had a bunch of follow-up appointments here, including imaging,” Breslow said via MLB.com . “We’re still collecting information, still working through what the kind of right course of treatment is. And at this point, it doesn’t seem that there’s any type of surgical intervention. It looks like rest is likely the best path to recovery.” Because of the wrist injury, Anthony could only take 242 plate appearances, finishing with an OPS of just .735. With Anthony set to be re-evaluated in a couple of weeks, the Red Sox hope the outfielder will be ready to participate in spring training in 2027. item.description: Jake Paul - Cedric Doumbe Credit: Most Valuable Promotions Has Jake Paul found his Rico Verhoeven? And is that a good or bad thing? Whenever a matchup is established or targeted, promoters have a responsibility to find the story angles and parallels that can be drawn. With MVP’s recent merger with PFL, it makes sense for Paul to target a wll-known combat sports athlete like Cedric Doumbé. He is someone MVP can easily negotiate with because there’s already a connection or a working relationship. Paul is also coming back after suffering a broken jaw in his 2025 loss against Anthony Joshua. With Doumbé having already fought for PFL, being a little up there in age, and being open to crossover combat sports events, he makes sense as an opponent. The Verhoeven connection is part of the promotional story. Verhoeven’s success against Oleksandr Usyk , and connecting Doumbé to him because of their similar backgrounds, is a way of essentially telling the public: Look at what happened when Verhoeven fought Usyk. No one gave him a chance. Now we have a similar fighter with a similar background facing a prominent fighter in Paul, and there’s reason to believe Doumbé could do what Verhoeven did, or better. That’s the story, and it doesn’t have to be a trick or a ruse. It could actually have some merit. Paul is a lot less experienced and skilled than Usyk. item.title: Aaron Judge Injury Update: Yankees GM Gives Major Details on NY Captain’s Health
item.description: Aaron Judge - NY Yankees | © Imagn New York Yankees captain Aaron Judge missed significant time in the regular season with a rib injury and then missed the entire postseason with a calf strain. Judge is expected to recover in the offseason and return for 2027 spring training. In Tuesday’s press conference, Yankees general manager Brian Cashman provided the latest update on Judge’s offseason recovery. “Aaron Judge had his follow-up with Dr. Pearl, which I think at the last Zoom call I had that we had said was yet to have happened and has happened, and he’s currently in a good place,” Cashman told reporters via SNY . “So no new added features to his circumstance outside of taking the winter to continue to rest up, and he’ll be ready to go. But there are no new procedures or anything there with Aaron Judge.” The update suggests that Judge’s follow-up appointment with Dr. Gregory Pearl to evaluate his recovery was good and that the Yankees star will not require any offseason procedure. In the regular season, Judge missed 84 games because of a right rib fracture. Then, in the last month of the regular season, Judge suffered a moderate-grade strain of his right soleus muscle in the Sept. 16 game against the Minnesota Twins. Before Judge could return in the postseason, the Yankees were swept in the ALDS against the Rays. Yankees GM Reveals Major Aaron Judge Role Change Ahead of 2027 MLB Season At MLB’s annual general managers’ meetings on Monday, Brian Cashman acknowledged the need to play Aaron Judge as designated hitter to better manage his workload and injuries. Judge’s availability in the lineup is more important to the Yankees than his everyday presence in right field. “I’m sure he’s going to need some DH times,” Cashman said . “I’m sure he doesn’t want to hear that. He’s an alpha, wants to play every day. It’s in his best interest, and what’s in his best interest is going to be what’s in our best interest.” Cashman’s comments throw the Yankees into a dilemma because they already have Giancarlo Stanton playing the everyday DH role. So, accommodating both of them in the usual setting might be difficult. Like Judge, Stanton is also recovering from his injuries and is expected to return by 2027 spring training. However, managing Judge’s workload throughout the season is important for the Yankees as the slugger will turn 35 in April 2027. His health remains the franchise’s biggest priority as they push for the World Series next season. item.description: Jayson Tatum celebrates after dunking on LeBron James © X/ @celtics Jayson Tatum gave everyone flashbacks to his rookie-season dunk on LeBron James on Tuesday. In the third quarter of the Boston Celtics’ 123-101 win over the Philadelphia 76ers, Tatum drew Joel Embiid out of the paint on a ball screen, opening up a window to attack the rim. James was the last line of the Sixers’ defense, and even though he wasn’t in the best position to contest Tatum’s attempt, he went for it and got posterized by the Celtics superstar. Tatum made his first statement play as a rookie in 2018 in Game 7 of the Eastern Conference Finals between the Celtics and Cavaliers with this dunk on James: Not many people can say they’ve posterized James, but Tatum has two such moments after Tuesday night. Almost everyone who watched Tatum dunk on Tuesday remembered the play from eight years ago. “Nobody likes dunking on LeBron James more than Jayson Tatum. Nobody,” one fan said. Jayson Tatum keeps it respectful while describing second poster on LeBron James While fans rallied behind Jayson Tatum for his dunk on LeBron James, the Celtics superstar humbly revisited the play after the game. Tatum said he was satisfied he could finish through all that contact and that it was just another basketball play. “It just kinda felt good to finish through contact,” he said during his walk-off interview with NBC. “It’s been about 19 months, you know, since I dunked on somebody, so just to kinda get my legs back, feeling good, you know. It’s a basketball play.” Tatum spent nearly 10 months recovering from an Achilles tear he suffered in May 2025 in the playoffs against the Knicks. He made a remarkable recovery and returned in March 2026 to finish the season. After a healthy 2026 offseason and a chance to play from opening night, Tatum is looking more comfortable and explosive with each game. On Tuesday, he finished with 21 points, six rebounds, and four assists, shooting 47.1%, including 3-for-7 from deep. Tatum took a step back offensively with his new co-star, Paul George, torching his former team with 36 points on 63.6% shooting.
